q: (Only Allaah knows the correct meaning of these letters.)
v.s: Alif, Lām, Meem.
v.c: Alif-Lãm-Mĩm.

q: There is no doubt in this revealed Book
from the Rabb of the universe.
v.s: [This is] the revelation of the Book about which there is no doubt from the Lord of the worlds.
v.c: The revelation of this Book is—beyond doubt—from the Lord of all worlds.

q: is the truth from your Rabb
has not come before you, so that they may be rightly guided
v.s: Or do they say, “He invented it”? Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, [O Muhammad], that you may warn a people to whom no warner has come before you [so] perhaps they will be guided.
v.c: Or do they say, “He has fabricated it!”? No! It is the truth from your Lord in order for you to warn a people to whom no warner has come before you, so they may be ˹rightly˺ guided.

q: It is Allaah Who created the heavens, the earth and whatever is between the two in six days and then turned His attention to the Throne. Besides Him, you have no Protecting Friend, nor any intercessor.
v.s: It is God who created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them in six days; then He established Himself above the Throne. You have not besides Him any protector or any intercessor; so will you not be reminded?
v.c: It is Allah Who has created the heavens and the earth and everything in between in six Days, then established Himself on the Throne. You have no protector or intercessor besides Him. Will you not then be mindful?

q: directs every affair from the heavens to the earth
(whatever He has decided shall take place on earth),
the duration of which is a thousand years according to your count
v.s: He arranges [each] matter from the heaven to the earth; then it will ascend to Him in a Day, the extent of which is a thousand years of those which you count.
v.c: He conducts every affair from the heavens to the earth, then it all ascends to Him on a Day whose length is a thousand years by your counting.

q: He Who has knowledge of the unseen and the seen. He is Mighty
v.s: That is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Exalted in Might, the Merciful,
v.c: That is the Knower of the seen and unseen—the Almighty, Most Merciful,

q: of everything and originated the creation of man
v.s: Who perfected everything which He created and began the creation of man from clay.
v.c: Who has perfected everything He created. And He originated the creation of humankind from clay.

q: from a product of lowly water
v.s: Then He made his posterity out of the extract of a liquid disdained.
v.c: Then He made his descendants from an extract of a humble fluid,

q: in him, and granted you ears, eyes and hearts. Little is the gratitude you show
(for all these great favours which none other can give).
v.s: Then He proportioned him and breathed into him from His [created] soul and made for you hearing and vision and hearts [i.e., intellect]; little are you grateful.
v.c: then He fashioned them and had a spirit of His Own ˹creation˺ breathed into them. And He gave you hearing, sight, and intellect. ˹Yet˺ you hardly give any thanks.

q: will we really be created again?” The fact is that they
(are not merely questioning to inquire, but they totally)
reject the meeting with their Rabb
(and will not accept it even if given a convincing answer).
v.s: And they say, “When we are lost [i.e., disintegrated] within the earth, will we indeed be [recreated] in a new creation?” Rather, they are, in [the matter of] the meeting with their Lord, disbelievers.
v.c: ˹Still˺ they ask ˹mockingly˺, “When we are disintegrated into the earth, will we really be raised as a new creation?” In fact, they are in denial of the meeting with their Lord.

q: (to them in reply), “(The affair will not be as easy as merely becoming part of the earth.)
The angel of death, who is appointed over you, will
(when the time for your death arrives and you will suffer terribly),
after which you will be returned to your Rabb
(to account for your actions and beliefs in this world and then be punished).”
v.s: Say, “The angel of death will take you who has been entrusted with you. Then to your Lord you will be returned.”
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Your soul will be taken by the Angel of Death, who is in charge of you. Then to your Lord you will ˹all˺ be returned.”

q: If only they could see the scene
will bow their heads before their Rabb
(everything that we refused to believe when Your Ambiyaa mentioned them to us).
carry out good deeds. We are now certainly convinced
(about everything that the Ambiyaa told us).” (Of course, this plea will be rejected because no one will be sent back to the world after death.)
v.s: If you could but see when the criminals are hanging their heads before their Lord, [saying], "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us [to the world]; we will work righteousness. Indeed, we are [now] certain."
v.c: If only you could see the wicked hanging their heads ˹in shame˺ before their Lord, ˹crying:˺ “Our Lord! We have now seen and heard, so send us back and we will do good. We truly have sure faith ˹now˺!”

v.s: And if We had willed, We could have given every soul its guidance, but the word from Me will come into effect [that] "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together.
v.c: Had We willed, We could have easily imposed guidance on every soul. But My Word will come to pass: I will surely fill up Hell with jinn and humans all together.

v.s: So taste [punishment] because you forgot the meeting of this, your Day; indeed, We have [accordingly] forgotten you. And taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do."
v.c: So taste ˹the punishment˺ for neglecting the meeting of this Day of yours. We ˹too˺ will certainly neglect you. And taste the torment of eternity for what you used to do!

v.s: Only those believe in Our verses who, when they are reminded by them, fall down in prostration and exalt [God] with praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant.
v.c: The only ˹true˺ believers in Our revelation are those who—when it is recited to them—fall into prostration and glorify the praises of their Lord and are not too proud.

v.s: Their sides part [i.e., they arise] from [their] beds; they supplicate their Lord in fear and aspiration, and from what We have provided them, they spend.
v.c: They abandon their beds, invoking their Lord with hope and fear, and donate from what We have provided for them.

v.s: And no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes [i.e., satisfaction] as reward for what they used to do.
v.c: No soul can imagine what delights are kept in store for them as a reward for what they used to do.

v.s: Then is one who was a believer like one who was defiantly disobedient? They are not equal.
v.c: Is the one who is a believer equal ˹before Allah˺ to the one who is rebellious? They are not equal!

q: As for those who have Imaan and who do good deeds, as hospitality for them, there shall be Jannaat
v.s: As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them will be the Gardens of Refuge as accommodation for what they used to do.
v.c: As for those who believe and do good, they will have the Gardens of ˹Eternal˺ Residence—as an accommodation for what they used to do.

q: As for those who are sinful, their abode shall be the Fire. Each time they attempt to come out of it, they will be returned to it
and told, “Taste of the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny
v.s: But as for those who defiantly disobeyed, their refuge is the Fire. Every time they wish to emerge from it, they will be returned to it while it is said to them, "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny."
v.c: But as for those who are rebellious, the Fire will be their home. Whenever they try to escape from it, they will be forced back into it, and will be told, “Taste the Fire’s torment, which you used to deny.”

m: And surely, We will let them taste
q: We shall definitely let them taste the closer
(to the path of Imaan and righteousness).
v.s: And We will surely let them taste the nearer punishment short of the greater punishment that perhaps they will return [i.e., repent].
v.c: We will certainly make them taste some of the minor torment ˹in this life˺ before the major torment ˹of the Hereafter˺, so perhaps they will return ˹to the Right Path˺.

q: Who is more unjust than he who is reminded of the Aayaat of his Rabb and then turns away from them
We will certainly take revenge on (punish) the criminals
v.s: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord; then he turns away from them? Indeed We, from the criminals, will take retribution.
v.c: And who does more wrong than the one who is reminded of Allah’s revelations then turns away from them? We will surely inflict punishment upon the wicked.

q: never be in doubt about receiving it
(the Qur'aan because you have also received it in a like manner).
(just as the Qur'aan is a means of guidance for all the people of your Ummah).
v.s: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture, so do not be in doubt over his meeting. And We made it [i.e., the Torah] guidance for the Children of Israel.
v.c: Indeed, We gave the Scripture to Moses—so let there be no doubt ˹O Prophet˺ that you ˹too˺ are receiving revelations—and We made it a guide for the Children of Israel.

q: We made leaders who guided under Our command when they exercised sabr
v.s: And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and [when] they were certain of Our signs.
v.c: We raised from among them leaders, guiding by Our command, when they patiently endured and firmly believed in Our signs.

q: Indeed, only your Rabb shall decide between them on the Day of Qiyaamah concerning the matters about which they differed.
v.s: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
v.c: Indeed, your Lord will decide between them on the Day of Judgment regarding their differences.

q: not been guided by the fact that We destroyed so many generations before them, in whose settlements
in this. Do they not listen?
(Do they not realise that they will suffer the same fate as these people for rejecting Imaan?)
v.s: Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, [as] they walk among their dwellings? Indeed in that are signs; then do they not hear?
v.c: Is it not yet clear to them how many peoples We destroyed before them, whose ruins they still pass by? Surely in this are signs. Will they not then listen?

q: not see that We draw water
plants from which your animals and you eat? Do they not see
(that just as We revive dead land, We can easily revive dead bodies on the Day of Qiyaamah)?
v.s: Have they not seen that We drive the water [in clouds] to barren land and bring forth thereby crops from which their livestock eat and [they] themselves? Then do they not see?
v.c: Do they not see how We drive rain to parched land, producing ˹various˺ crops from which they and their cattle eat? Will they not then see?

q: (the punishment to separate yourselves from us)
take place if you are truthful?”
v.s: And they say, "When will be this conquest, if you should be truthful?"
v.c: They ask ˹mockingly˺, “When is this ˹Day of final˺ Decision, if what you say is true?”

q: Say, “On the day of the decision, the Imaan of the Kuffaar will be of no help to them
neither will they be granted respite
(any further opportunity to lead proper lives as Mu'mineen).”
v.s: Say, [O Muhammad], “On the Day of Conquest the belief of those who had disbelieved will not benefit them, nor will they be reprieved.”
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “On the Day of Decision it will not benefit the disbelievers to believe then, nor will they be delayed ˹from punishment˺.”

q: (since they refuse to be convinced despite your sincerest efforts, you should rather)
turn away from them and wait
(for Allaah's punishment to overtake them because)
v.s: So turn away from them and wait. Indeed, they are waiting.
v.c: So turn away from them, and wait! They too are waiting.
